thread:
sylvia: Starting iad3 GPU cluster networking bring-up. Main goals: TGW peering to core transit account, BGP session with partner transit for cross-region replication, scaleable NAT for model pulls, and private DNS delegation for *.models.redwood.internal. Want a short checklist and owners for each step.
omar: I'll take TGW peering + route filters. Key callouts: need BGP community tagging so partner doesn't accept our internal-only routes. Also we should avoid leaking private 10.0.0.0/8 outside core.
lee: I'll own the NAT autoscale design and cost guardrails. Plan is: ephemeral NAT fleet (ASG) + managed NAT gateways for steady-state, plus egress metering tag.
maria: I'll handle Route53 delegation and private hosted zone setup. Confirming: core account will create a delegation record to our account's private zone, right?
sylvia: yes — core will add NS delegation to zone iad3.models.redwood.internal pointing to the VPC's Resolver endpoints. maria, add validation steps for split-horizon.
ethan: For BGP, partner requires MD5 and prefix limits. Also need to tag routes with community 65535:100 to mark them as internal-only. Can someone validate community support on partner side?
omar: Partner side confirmed community acceptance via today's call. We'll also add route filters to TGW attachments: deny 0.0.0.0/0 learned from peer, allow only 10/16 and 172.16/12 ranges.
jack: small note: kernel panic we hit on iad2 during NAT burst was due to conntrack exhaustion. Lee, we should include conntrack tuning in the runbook.
lee: good catch. Runbook will include sysctl adjustments and a Prom rule for conntrack usage > 90% -> scale up NAT ASG. Also add a cooldown for scale-down.
deploy-bot: terraform apply complete: tgws/iad3-tgw created (tgw-0a1b2c3d), vpc attachments pending. Plan id: plan-20260318-01
sylvia: Omar, coordinate the attachment handoff with cloudops since this requires cross-account role assumption. Also please include the exact IAM role and permissions for the attachment.
omar: will do. IAM role is arn:aws:iam::COREACCOUNT:role/TGW-Attach-Role with permission to ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment, ec2:ModifyTransitGatewayVpcAttachment. I'll post the policy block in the runbook.
maria: DNS notes: create private zone iad3.models.redwood.internal in our account, create A records for service discovery pointing to internal ELBs and NLBs. Add health check for the model registry endpoint. Then share NS records with core.
ethan: BGP config snippet for edge routers: ```neighbor 10.0.254.1 remote-as 65001 password md5_password! neighbor 10.0.254.1 prefix-list INBOUND in``` Also include `neighbor x route-map SET-COMMUNITY out` to add 65535:100.
lee: NAT sizing: estimate steady egress 800 Mbps, peaks 6 Gbps during model pulls. Suggest 2 x managed NAT gw for 1 Gbps steady + ASG of c6gn.large NAT boxes for burst with iptables SNAT. We'll use Elastic IP pool and rotation to avoid per-IP rate limits from cloud providers.
jack: add firewall rule to only allow egress to allowed registries (registry.redwood.ai, ghcr.io). Helps reduce outbound noise and unexpected flows.
sylvia: Good. Also add cost-control: tag all egress flows with billing tag `cost-center:gpu-iad3`. Lee, add alert for NAT spend > $X/day.
lee: done — I'll add a daily burnrate alert and an automated throttling policy: if projected daily NAT cost > budget, switch non-essential hosts to cached registry and pause model prefetch.
omar: Routing validation checklist (short): 1) TGW route tables correct for VPC attachment 2) BGP session UP and prefixes matched 3) Route filters in place 4) No 0.0.0.0/0 leaked 5) Blackhole detection (route53 health checks)
maria: DNS validation: 1) Private zone resolution from worker subnets 2) Delegation NS visible in core account 3) Split-horizon test: public lookup should not resolve internal hosts 4) Internal health checks pass for registry
ethan: Add a test plan for BGP failover: simulate partner circuit down, ensure TGW falls back to alternate transit and routes still prefer local egress for small control-plane traffic.
jack: Ops handoff: oncall rotation for first 72h will be eng-infra primary (sylvia) then SRE (jack) for 1 week. Add runbook link and pager runbook to the thread.
oncall-bot: Pager schedule updated: sylvia oncall 2026-03-18 12:00 -> 2026-03-21 12:00 UTC, escalation to jack after 30m.
sylvia: Final ask: please add short troubleshooting snippets to the runbook: common BGP commands, `ip route` checks, `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`, how to rotate EIPs for NAT ASG, and the terraform import commands for TGW attachments.
omar: I'll add a section with commands: ```# check TGW attachments aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=tgw-0a1b2c3d``` and BGP neighbor status on edge: `show ip bgp summary`
maria: I'll add DNS dig examples and a curl example that hits the registry via internal LB.
lee: I'll add conntrack tuning: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000` and Prom rule example.
ethan: Will add BGP show config and how to import peers into our monitoring.
sylvia: Great. Once runbook is updated, we do a dry run with Cloudops in the staging account, then schedule a low-traffic maintenance window to flip production. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
jack: Thanks — leaving notes for post-mortem if anything weird happens.
deploy-bot: smoke test passed: internal DNS resolution ok, NAT connectivity to registry.ok, BGP session established with partner, minor flapping observed -> set bgp dampening lower threshold. Logs: plan-20260318-01 -> apply-id-7f3a
lee: saw conntrack climb to 82% during smoke — autoscale kicked correctly. Will tweak cooldowns after observing 24h.
sylvia: closing the thread after runbook PR merged. Please ping here if you hit any blockers during the dry-run.
